name: The Sāṃkhya Kārikā's path from suffering to isolation

stages.name: jijñāsā
stages.description: Struck by the three sufferings and finding seen remedies uncertain and impermanent, one seeks their destroyer.

stages.name: turning from Vedic means
stages.description: Vedic means are impure, perishable and graded; discriminating knowledge is better.

stages.name: approaching the teacher; study, hearing, reasoning
stages.description: Study, hearing, reasoning, a knowing friend and service to the venerable bring knowledge of the principles; error, incapacity and contentment are abandoned.

stages.name: tattvābhyāsa
stages.description: Long, reverent, uninterrupted contemplation of the principles.

stages.name: nāsmi na me nāham
stages.gloss: 'I am not, not mine, not I'
stages.description: The complete, pure, single discriminating knowledge arises.

stages.name: prakṛti ceases for the seer
stages.description: Puruṣa sees prakṛti, her purpose served, withdrawn like a dancer; no motive for further creation remains.

stages.name: dhṛtaśarīra
stages.description: Virtue and the rest no longer cause; the knower remains embodied by the momentum of impressions, like a potter's wheel.

stages.name: kaivalya
stages.description: At the body's end, pradhāna having ceased, final isolation.

name: The Sāṃkhya Sūtra's path of meditation and discrimination

stages.name: hearing instruction repeatedly
stages.description: Instruction in the truth (like the king's son), repeated, with reflection; mere hearing is not enough because latent tendencies are strong.

stages.name: one's own duty, posture, concentration, breath
stages.description: Performing the duties of one's stage of life, steady and pleasant posture, concentration, restraint by expulsion and retention; dispassion and practice.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: Cessation of mental modifications; mind without object; turning from torpor and distraction.

stages.name: tattvābhyāsa by 'neti neti'
stages.description: Giving up each principle with 'not this, not this'.

stages.name: vivekasiddhi
stages.description: Discrimination of puruṣa and prakṛti; liberation comes from knowledge alone.

stages.name: jīvanmukti
stages.description: Experience continues by residual impressions, like a whirling wheel; the liberated living teach.

stages.name: kṛtakṛtyatā
stages.description: Complete cessation of suffering through discrimination.

notes: Stages ordered from the sūtras' own sequence; bands are interpretive.
